channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Renan Santos defende PEC da transição para tratar de Previdência ainda este ano
item.description: Renan Santos, the Missão party's presidential candidate, stated on Monday (17) that a transitional Constitutional Amendment Proposal (PEC) must be approved this year to address pension-related issues. The remarks were made during the 27th Annual Santander Conference in São Paulo.

item.title: Aprovação de Lula cai abaixo de 30% no Lulômetro
item.description: President Lula's approval rating dropped below 30% in the Lulômetro, with 29% rating his performance as 'excellent' or 'good', 33% as 'fair', and 36% as 'bad' or 'terrible'. The survey, conducted by Realtime Big Data and O Antagonista, indicates a declining trend in his popularity.

item.title: 45% veem possível interferência estrangeira nas eleições, diz Quaest
item.description: According to a Quaest survey released on August 17, 2026, 45% of Brazilian voters believe foreign interference in the 2026 elections is possible, while 48% consider it impossible. Among Bolsonaro supporters, 64% see interference as possible and 71% believe it would benefit right-wing candidates; among Lula supporters, 60% dismiss the possibility, and 54% of those who see it as possible believe it would favor right-wing candidates. The survey interviewed 2,004 voters aged 16 and older between August 10–13, 2026, with a margin of error of ±2 percentage points at a 95% confidence level.

item.title: Afiliado político diz que Dino "será presidente da República"
item.description: Felipe Camarão, PT candidate for governor of Maranhão and self-declared political godson of Flávio Dino, stated in a podcast interview that the STF minister 'will be president of the Republic, if God wills it'. He praised Dino as one of the country's most brilliant minds and the greatest governor in Maranhão's history, crediting his own political trajectory to Dino's mentorship.

item.title: Haddad faz propostas para mulheres em primeiro ato da campanha ao governo de SP
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) launched his São Paulo gubernatorial campaign with a walk through the city center alongside his Senate candidates Simone Tebet (PSB) and Marina Silva (Rede). He emphasized policies targeting female voters, including extending hours at women’s police stations and creating a cross-agency communication hub to detect domestic violence early. Haddad also stood by his driver’s claim of being followed by a police vehicle, contradicting the state security secretary’s assertion that over 70 cameras found no evidence.

item.title: Durigan espera retomada da relação com EUA após as eleições
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan said he expects the resumption of dialogue and trade flow between Brazil and the United States after the October elections, describing current issues as punctual. He criticized the 37.5% additional tariffs imposed by the U.S. on Brazilian products, arguing it makes no sense to penalize Brazil when the country runs a trade deficit with the U.S. Durigan also defended Brazil’s independent foreign policy stance, rejecting automatic alignment with any power and advocating for diversified trade partnerships.

item.title: Maioria dos eleitores rejeita uso de inteligência artificial em campanhas, aponta Quaest
item.description: According to a Genial/Quaest survey, 73% of Brazilian voters disapprove of the use of artificial intelligence in electoral campaigns for 2026. The strong resistance reflects concerns about manipulation, misinformation, and loss of authenticity in politics.

item.title: Candidaturas de militares caem pela primeira vez desde 2002
item.description: For the first time since 2002, the number of military candidates in Brazilian elections has declined, dropping from 5.1% to 4.5% of the total. Out of 20,501 registered candidates, 921 use military ranks in their ballot names or declare affiliation with security forces. The decrease signals a weakening presence of military figures in electoral politics.

item.title: Idade média dos candidatos chega a 49,5 anos e mantém tendência de alta
item.description: The average age of candidates in the 2026 elections reached 49.5 years, continuing the upward trend observed over recent decades. The data was compiled by UOL based on information released by the Superior Electoral Court (TSE).

item.title: TSE admite ação contra Lula por suposto abuso em desfile de Carnaval
item.description: The TSE’s Corregedor-General, Minister Antonio Carlos Ferreira, admitted an action against President Lula and Vice President Geraldo Alckmin for alleged economic power abuse and improper use of communication media during Rio’s 2026 Carnival. The lawsuit, filed by the Novo party, claims the Acadêmicos de Niterói samba school received R$9.65 million in public funds after announcing its Lula-themed parade, while Lula was a pre-candidate for re-election. The minister found sufficient grounds to proceed and ordered Lula and Alckmin to present a defense within five days.

item.title: Marçal avisou Flávio sobre candidatura: “Você não terá problema comigo”
item.description: Pablo Marçal, PRTB presidential candidate, stated he does not intend to act as a 'shield' for any other candidate in the 2026 election and said he called Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) to inform him of his candidacy, adding that he will not have problems with him. Marçal emphasized that Flávio is the only candidate with whom he maintains a relationship of respect and understanding.

item.title: “Direitos humanos têm que ser para humanos direitos”, diz Nikolas Ferreira
item.description: Federal Deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) praised El Salvador's security policy under Nayib Bukele, stating that human rights must be for 'human rights' and criticizing NGOs for allegedly protecting criminals. He advocated adopting similar measures in Brazil, such as maximum-security prisons and lowering the age of criminal responsibility, but noted this depends on electing aligned lawmakers. Ferreira campaigned in Juiz de Fora (MG) supporting local candidates like Roberta Lopes, despite Flávio Bolsonaro's absence due to weather-related travel issues.

item.title: Sandro Alex declara apoio a Caiado, mas evita se distanciar de Flávio
item.description: Sandro Alex, the PSD candidate for governor of Paraná, declared his support for Ronaldo Caiado as his presidential pick in a UOL/Folha interview, yet avoided distancing himself from Flávio Bolsonaro and reiterated his backing of Jair Bolsonaro's government.

item.title: Em discurso a jato, Carlos Bolsonaro pede união da direita em meio a divergências no PL de SC
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro called for unity among Santa Catarina's right-wing in a brief speech alongside Governor Jorginho Mello, praising the governor's four-year record and urging his re-election. The appeal came amid internal divisions within the state's PL party, particularly with Deputy Ana Campagnolo, who has criticized Carlos Bolsonaro's Senate candidacy and his choice of running mate. Other ticket members, including Carol de Toni and Jorginho Mello, echoed the message of party cohesion.

item.title: O erro de Flávio Bolsonaro ao se comparar ao filho de Pelé
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro made a political misstep by comparing himself to Pelé’s son during the launch of his presidential campaign, drawing criticism for attempting to leverage the football legend’s fame to bolster his image. The comparison was seen as inappropriate and forced, given the lack of meaningful parallel between his political career and Pelé’s sporting legacy. The incident occurred amid efforts to reconnect with voters but instead highlighted poor political judgment.

item.title: Haddad faz caminhada no Centro de SP como 1º ato de campanha
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) launched his street campaign in São Paulo with a walk through the city center, joined by allies Marcio França, Simone Tebet and Marina Silva, emphasizing public security policies focused on women, health and education. He opposed the privatization and militarization of public schools, advocating for teacher valorization and quality learning, while pledging not to reverse existing educational policies. The Vox Brazil poll shows Tarcísio de Freitas leading with 53.7% and Haddad with 34% in the first round for São Paulo governor.

item.title: Lula de chapéu: presidente diz que adotou adereço por causa de tratamento de câncer de pele na cabeça
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva revealed he is wearing a Panama hat due to radiotherapy treatment for skin cancer on his head, following surgery in April. Despite medical advice to avoid sun exposure, he stated he will remove the hat to greet supporters during the opening event of his re-election campaign in São Bernardo do Campo. The decision to wear the hat in the electronic ballot photo has raised concerns among allies about potential legal challenges at the TSE, although recent precedents authorize cultural accessories if they do not hinder voter identification.

item.title: Campanha de Tarcísio avalia abandonar jingle de Latino após acusação
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas' re-election campaign is considering dropping the jingle 'Tarcísio me leva', inspired by a song from singer Latino, following allegations of assault made by his ex-wife, Raffa Rarbbie. The jingle, used since 2022 and updated for the 2026 campaign, may harm the candidate's image amid efforts to appeal to female voters. The move comes after a formal meeting with women in Osasco and amid evidence of prior contact between Tarcísio and Latino, including a dinner in August 2023.

item.title: Crusoé: Brasileiro mente sobre debate nas pesquisas
item.description: A BTG/Nexus poll released on March 17, 2025, shows that 86% of Brazilians claim they will watch the presidential debates on television. The article suggests this high figure may reflect a social desirability bias — wanting to appear informed — rather than genuine intent to follow the debates, pointing to a possible gap between stated intentions and actual behavior.

item.title: Pelo PT, Lula busca reeleição com foco em pautas sociais
item.description: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, 80, is seeking re-election as President of Brazil for the Workers' Party (PT), with Geraldo Alckmin as his running mate. His career is defined by union leadership, founding the PT in 1980, and governing with a focus on social policies, poverty reduction, and state-led economic development. Lula previously served as president from 2003 to 2010 and returned in 2023, aiming to become the first Brazilian president elected three times.

item.title: Plano de Tarcísio prevê obras nas periferias, escolas cívico-militares e linha de crédito para mães
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans) filed his re-election government plan, emphasizing infrastructure projects in peripheral areas, expansion of civic-military schools, and a credit and voucher program for entrepreneurial mothers. The plan also includes broadening technical education, introducing AI literacy courses, and prioritizing infrastructure that connects peripheries to job centers. Cited achievements from his first term include ending Cracolândia, expanding water access via Sabesp privatization, and delivering road and rail projects.

item.title: Janja escondeu elogio a Marisa para fazer surpresa a Lula e 'virar página' com petistas
item.description: First Lady Janja revealed she reserved her praise for former First Lady Marisa Letícia to a small, close group during Lula’s campaign launch in São Bernardo do Campo, intending to surprise the president and 'move on' with the PT base.

item.title: Flávio mantém agenda em BH após cancelar em Juiz de Fora; veja onde
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro canceled his campaign event in Juiz de Fora after his aircraft was denied landing authorization, but confirmed his attendance at the Belo Horizonte rally launching the Flávio Roscoe and Ellen Miziara ticket on Monday evening (17/8). The event will take place at 7 p.m. at Mackenzie College Gymnasium in the Santo Antônio neighborhood, attended by PL leaders including Domingos Sávio and Nikolas Ferreira.

item.title: Leia a troca de mensagens entre Lulinha e Roberta sobre a “Suíça”
item.description: Federal Police intercepted messages between Fábio Luís da Silva (Lulinha), son of President Lula, and lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, revealing business dealings involving a future in Switzerland, meetings with former Lula aides such as Marcola and Berger, and alleged links to businessman Antonio Carlos Camilo Antunes, investigated for attempting a medicinal cannabis contract with SUS. The messages also mention Fernando Bittar, Lulinha’s former partner, trying to use Lula’s name to secure Telebras deals, and reiterate prior discussions about using tax havens like Luxembourg to evade federal revenue authorities.

item.title: Justiça rejeita denúncia criminal contra Ricardo Nunes por chamar promotor de 'idiota'
item.description: The 2nd Criminal Chamber of the São Paulo State Court of Justice unanimously rejected (3-0) a criminal complaint against Mayor Ricardo Nunes (MDB) for calling a prosecutor an 'idiot' during a public event. The court ruled that, although the remark was offensive, it did not constitute the crimes of insult or defamation under Brazilian Penal Code, as it occurred in the context of public debate and lacked the specific intent to harm the prosecutor’s honor.

item.title: Com 2% nas pesquisas, Augusto Cury prepara cartas para Lula e Flávio
item.description: Augusto Cury, the Avante party's presidential candidate with 2% in polls, plans to personally deliver letters to Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) this week in Brasília, appealing for Brazil's 'pacification'. The letters will be handed over at the Planalto Palace and Flávio Bolsonaro's Senate office during his participation in debates in the capital. Cury shares the same 2% voting intention as Romeu Zema (Novo) in the latest Quaest poll.

item.title: Ministro do TSE fala em contexto desafiador com evolução da IA
item.description: TSE Minister Nauê Bernardo warned of the risks posed by the rapid evolution of Artificial Intelligence amid low digital literacy in Brazil, stating that delegating strategic decisions to algorithms threatens democracy. He introduced the concept of 'algorithmic degradation' and emphasized that Brazil lives in a 'risk society', per Ulrich Beck, requiring urgent understanding of technological consequences to safeguard institutions.

item.title: Sem Flávio, Nikolas faz campanha em Juiz de Fora e critica Lula
item.description: Federal Deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) conducted a street campaign in Juiz de Fora (MG) after Flávio Bolsonaro's visit was canceled, criticizing President Lula and the federal government over high tax burden, rising food prices, and foreign policy. He praised international right-wing leaders Javier Milei and Nayib Bukele, advocating for direct grassroots campaigning to win over undecided voters.

item.title: Tendência é de baixa renovação no Congresso
item.description: Most federal deputies are seeking re-election in 2026, with 84.6% having registered candidacies, indicating low renewal in Congress. States like Paraíba, Piauí, and Rio Grande do Norte show 100% of deputies running again, compared to renewal rates of 39.38% in 2022 and 47.37% in 2018. Meanwhile, investigations involve Lulinha and lobbyists, while polls show Lula leading in the first round but technically tied with Flávio Bolsonaro and Ronaldo Caiado in the second.

item.title: Dino afasta sobrinho de Carlos Brandão da presidência do Tribunal de Contas do Maranhão
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino ordered a 180-day removal of Daniel Brandão, president of Maranhão’s Court of Accounts and nephew of Governor Carlos Brandão, over suspicions of involvement in a murder and a parliamentary amendment embezzlement scheme. The ruling cites evidence of financial transfers, cash payments, and use of front men to conceal Daniel’s role, along with risks of political favoritism toward his uncle. The case also involves Senator Weverton Rocha allegedly pressuring the STJ to obstruct the investigation.

item.title: TSE nega ação contra Flávio por visita de Milei e vídeo de IA de Bolsonaro
item.description: The Electoral Justice Corregedor, Minister Antonio Carlos Ferreira, rejected the request to open a Judicial Electoral Investigation Action against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro on technical grounds: the petitioner and the respondent were still pre-candidates at the time of filing, and such actions can only be assessed after official candidacy registration. Furthermore, the petitioner did not run for the same office (president), lacking active and passive legitimacy. The AI-generated video of Bolsonaro will be examined in a separate action filed by the Workers' Party (PT).

item.title: Internacional x Remo no Brasileirão: onde assistir, horário e escalações
item.description: Internacional and Remo face off this Monday, the 17th, at 8:00 PM Brasília time, at Beira-Rio, in a direct clash for Série A survival. Colorado needs a win to escape the relegation zone, while Remo aims to surpass its rival in the standings. The match will be broadcast on SporTV and Premiere, with referee Edina Alves Batista in charge.

item.title: Nunes Marques assume defesa da urna em resposta aos EUA e a colegas do TSE
item.description: TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques convened ambassadors and diplomats for a closed meeting on Monday (17) to explain the security mechanisms of electronic voting machines and reinforce the credibility of Brazilian elections amid suspicions of foreign interference, particularly from the U.S. The meeting, planned since May, follows the denial of visas to two U.S. diplomats in July over alleged efforts to discredit the vote and statements by Flávio Bolsonaro linking the ballot box manufacturer to fraud in Venezuela, which the TSE had already denied. Marques aims to preempt international questioning and address internal court concerns, having established the Directorate of International Affairs to strengthen dialogue with foreign representatives.

item.title: Quaest: para 60% dos eleitores, partido do candidato influencia escolha de voto para presidente
item.description: A Quaest poll reveals that 60% of Brazilian voters say the candidate's party influences their presidential vote choice, with 38% stating it influences a lot and 22% saying it influences a little. Among independent voters (those not identifying with Lula, non-Lulist left, Bolsonaro, or non-Bolsonarist right), 50% say the party does not influence their vote, while 47% of Lulists and 48% of Bolsonarists say the party influences their choice a lot. The survey interviewed 2,004 people from August 10–13, with a 2-point margin of error and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Bolsonaro vira alma penada da sucessão presidencial de 2026
item.description: Despite being barred from political acts and social media, Jair Bolsonaro was the focal point of the first day of the 2026 election campaign. His symbolic presence, described as that of a 'wandering soul,' haunted venues like Vila Euclides stadium and Copacabana beach, even without appearing in person. The text emphasizes that neither Lula nor Flávio Bolsonaro were the protagonists of the campaign’s opening day.

item.title: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro tentam inflamar suas bases antes da disputa pelo eleitor de centro
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro launched their 2026 pre-campaigns by returning to their political strongholds to energize their bases: Lula in São Bernardo do Campo, invoking his union roots and historical legacy, and Flávio in Copacabana, reinforcing bolsonarist identity. Both aimed to rekindle militant enthusiasm before targeting centrist voters, using emotional symbolism and historical references to solidify internal support. Lula’s event emphasized past and present government achievements, though with little novelty, focusing on reinforcing PT identity and contrasting his administration with Bolsonaro’s.

item.title: ‘Hoje, até Lula me pediria para permanecer no Senado’, diz Marina Silva
item.description: Marina Silva, former Environment Minister and ex-senator from Acre, announced her candidacy for the Senate from São Paulo, stating she intends to serve the full term and that President Lula, if re-elected, would ask her to stay in the Senate due to the environmental agenda being at risk in Congress. She criticizes recent congressional changes to environmental licensing and the enforcement against illegal mining equipment, arguing that, had she been a senator, these measures would not have passed in their current form.

item.title: Marçal, Garotinho, Arruda: entenda por que candidatos inelegíveis ou com pendências conseguiram registrar candidatura
item.description: Candidates with judicial impediments or ineligibility, such as Pablo Marçal, Anthony Garotinho, Arthur Henrique, and José Roberto Arruda, managed to register their candidacies with the TSE, but their registrations remain under review by the Electoral Justice. Registration is merely the first procedural step and does not guarantee the right to run, as the TSE must still verify compliance with legal requirements. The TSE will assess each case after the August 15 registration deadline.

item.title: Remo desafia o Internacional em duelo na zona de rebaixamento
item.description: Internacional and Remo face off in the Brasileirão 2026 relegation zone, with Colorado needing to end a six-match winless streak. Remo, in 18th place, seeks its first away point against an Internacional side that last won 4-1 over Vasco in May. Betting odds favor Internacional (1.55), with strong likelihood of both teams scoring (1.91), based on recent head-to-head history.

item.title: Entenda o que são estrelas vermelhas e bandeira do Brasil no Instagram
item.description: On Sunday (August 16), supporters of Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) used emojis in Instagram's 'Notes' feature to show support in the 2022 elections. Lula's backers posted a golden star on a red background, referencing the PT flag, while Flávio's supporters used the Brazilian flag, associated with Jair Bolsonaro. Some also shared a funk containing offensive content against Lula.

item.title: TRE-DF defere primeira candidatura ao GDF
item.description: The TRE-DF approved the candidacy of Professor Robson (PSTU) for the Government of the Federal District, following a ruling by Judge André Puppin. The decision confirms that the candidate met all legal requirements for registration. This is Robson Raymundo da Silva’s second run for the GDF, having previously contested in 2022 and run for the Federal Senate in 2010, 2014, and 2018.

item.title: Em Copacabana e na Paulista, Flávio tenta retomar mobilização do pai contra baixa adesão nas ruas
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL presidential candidate, faces low turnout in his early campaign events, with only 8,900 people attending in Copacabana — far below the 64,600 his father, Jair Bolsonaro, drew in 2022. The absence of the former president, imprisoned for attempting a coup, has significantly reduced right-wing rally attendance, dropping from an average of 49,500 with him to 18,700 without him. Flávio aims to revive Bolsonarist street mobilization through events in Juiz de Fora and a themed rally on Avenida Paulista.

item.title: Mau tempo cancela agenda de Flávio Bolsonaro em Juiz de Fora
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro canceled his participation in a motorcycle rally in Juiz de Fora on Monday (17) after adverse weather conditions prevented his flight from Rio de Janeiro from taking off, specifically due to 'ceiling' restrictions. His campaign staff confirmed the cancellation, attributing it solely to poor weather. The event was part of his presidential campaign agenda.

item.title: Estreia esvaziada sem Michelle e Nikolas provoca críticas no PL e abre discussão sobre formato dos atos de Flávio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's debut street rally in Copacabana drew around 9,000 attendees, significantly fewer than the crowds mobilized by his father Jair Bolsonaro in past events, sparking internal criticism within the PL over the event's format. Despite the low physical turnout, the live stream reached approximately 35,000 simultaneous viewers, which allies cite as evidence of stronger digital mobilization. PL leadership acknowledges that the large allocated space made the low attendance more visible, suggesting a smaller venue or different location could have avoided the negative perception of emptiness.

item.title: Frozen abre nova era na Disneyland Paris para brasileiros
item.description: Disneyland Paris has become a central destination for Brazilian tourists in 2025, driven by the blend of classic Disney magic with contemporary franchises like Frozen. The park surpassed traditional attractions such as the Colosseum and Vatican in the ranking of most-purchased international tickets by Brazilians, signaling a shift from supplementary stop to primary motivator for European travel. The March 2026 expansion of Disney Adventure World, particularly the World of Frozen area, strengthens this multigenerational appeal by combining nostalgic affection with immersive modern experiences.

item.title: Dino afasta sobrinho de governador do Maranhão do Tribunal de Contas
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino ordered the 180-day precautionary removal of Daniel Itapary Brandão, nephew of Maranhão Governor Carlos Brandão, from his positions as councilor and president of the TCE-MA, amid a PF investigation into a suspected criminal organization diverting public funds, including federal parliamentary amendments, and obstructing inquiries. The order bars him from accessing tribunal systems, premises, assets, and contacting individuals linked to the investigation, including the governor and associates.

item.title: Patrimônio de Marçal salta para R$ 7,4 bilhões no registro eleitoral
item.description: The declared assets of Pablo Marçal for his 2026 presidential candidacy, filed with the TSE, amounted to R$ 7.4 billion. However, Marçal himself disputed the figure, telling Estadão that the declaration was incorrect and that he had already requested a correction. He did not disclose what the actual net worth should be.

item.title: TSE reúne mais de 100 diplomatas para explicar segurança das urnas
item.description: The TSE is hosting over 100 diplomats in Brasília to explain the functioning and security of Brazil's electronic voting system, including safeguards against deepfakes and disinformation. Minister Kassio Nunes Marques is presenting the step-by-step voting process and contingency plans for the 2026 elections. The meeting is part of a series since June aimed at reinforcing the transparency and credibility of Brazil's electoral process to the international community.

item.title: Eleição para Câmara dos Deputados terá menos candidatos neste ano
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian Chamber of Deputies elections will feature 7,620 candidates, down from 9,477 in 2022, with lower competition per seat and increased representation of women (37%), college-educated candidates (71%), and indigenous individuals (75). The decline stems from the abolition of party coalitions, the performance clause, and a 2021 election law limiting candidates per party to 100% of state seats plus one.

item.title: Voto em trânsito pode ser pedido até quinta-feira, 20: veja como usar o serviço
item.description: Voters outside their electoral domicile can request absentee voting until Thursday, August 20, to vote in another municipality during the 2026 elections. The request can be submitted online via the TSE’s Electronic Self-Service or in person at electoral offices, with options to select different turns and locations. The allowance permits voting for all offices only if remaining in the same state; in another state, only for president of the Republic.
